blocks.content: Unlike in the case of the Supreme Court, the Constitution makes no provision for the appointment of a distinguished jurist as a judge of a High Court.

items: The Constitution has NOT prescribed any minimum age for appointment as a judge of a High Court.
A 'distinguished jurist' can be appointed as a Supreme Court judge, but NOT as a High Court judge.
The retirement age of High Court judges was raised from 60 to 62 years by the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1963.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A candidate must be a citizen of India to be appointed as a High Court judge.
The candidate must have held a judicial office in the territory of India for at least ten years.
Alternatively, the candidate must have been an advocate of a High Court (or High Courts in succession) for at least ten years.
The Constitution does not prescribe any minimum age for appointment as a judge of a High Court.
Unlike the Supreme Court, there is no constitutional provision for appointing a 'distinguished jurist' as a High Court judge.
